wheel.name: Friction: the wheel at spread capture 0.50

rules.action: Sell on the first bar of the week's first session where the condition holds; if none does, sell nothing that week
rules.condition: The selected option has a valid bid and ask on the bar, and its spread is at most {max_spread:.0%} of its mid
rules.name: Entry trigger
rules.rationale: Liquidity decides when we trade, not a clock, and every fill is modeled at the mid, so a wide market would make that assumption unsafe. A week with no liquid bar is skipped rather than traded at a worse price.
rules.summary: On the first hourly bar of the week's first session where the option we picked has both a bid and an ask, and its spread is no wider than {max_spread:.0%} of mid.
rules.title: When in the session do we sell?

rules.action: Sell one put, chosen by the put expiry and strike rules, once the entry trigger passes
rules.condition: The week's first session, holding cash and no shares or options
rules.name: Put timing
rules.rationale: The wheel's first leg: we're paid to agree to buy the stock lower down. Selling at the start of the week gives the put the whole week's time value.
rules.summary: At the start of every week in which we hold only cash.
rules.title: When do we sell a put?

rules.action: Use the expiry on the week's last trading session (a Thursday in a holiday week)
rules.name: Put expiry
rules.rationale: Weekly options decay fastest in their last days, and a week-long put gives about 26 cycles in the backtest window, enough to judge the results.
rules.title: Which expiry do we sell the put in?

rules.action: Choose the put whose delta is nearest −{target_delta:.2f}; a tie goes to the lower strike
rules.condition: Puts with a strike below the stock's price on the bar and a delta solved from their mid
rules.name: Put strike
rules.rationale: A delta near −{target_delta:.2f} puts the strike a little below the stock: a premium worth collecting, and roughly a {target_delta:.0%} chance of being assigned the shares.
rules.summary: The out-of-the-money put whose delta is closest to −{target_delta:.2f}.
rules.title: Which put strike do we sell?

rules.action: Sell {contracts} contract and set that cash aside until the put expires or is assigned; otherwise sell nothing that week
rules.condition: Cash after the sale is at least the strike × 100 × {contracts} contract
rules.name: Cash-secured
rules.rationale: A cash-secured put can always be paid for if it's assigned: no margin, no leverage. The cash set aside earns nothing here.
rules.summary: {contracts} contract, sold only if cash covers buying the shares at the strike.
rules.title: How much do we sell, and how is it secured?

rules.action: Sell one call, chosen by the call expiry and strike rules, once the entry trigger passes
rules.condition: The week's first session, holding 100 shares and no option
rules.name: Call timing
rules.rationale: The wheel's second leg: once we own the shares, we're paid to agree to sell them higher up.
rules.summary: At the start of every week in which we hold the shares and no call.
rules.title: When do we sell a covered call?

rules.action: Use the expiry on the week's last trading session (a Thursday in a holiday week)
rules.name: Call expiry
rules.rationale: Weekly, like the put, so each week is one decision.
rules.title: Which expiry do we sell the call in?

rules.action: Choose the call whose delta is nearest {target_delta:.2f}; a tie goes to the higher strike. If no call qualifies, sell none that week
rules.condition: Calls with a strike above the stock's price on the bar, at or above the cost basis (the put strike less the put's credit and every call credit since, per share), and a delta solved from their mid
rules.name: Call strike
rules.rationale: Being called away below the cost basis would lock in a loss, so the floor comes first and the delta second. When the stock has fallen far below the basis, that can mean no call, or a small premium far out of the money.
rules.summary: The out-of-the-money call whose delta is closest to {target_delta:.2f}, but never below what the shares cost us, less the premiums collected since.
rules.title: Which call strike do we sell?

rules.action: Record the put as expired at $0 and release the cash set aside
rules.condition: At the expiry session's close, the stock's last trade is at or above the put's strike
rules.name: Put expires
rules.rationale: The best outcome for a put seller.
rules.summary: It expires worthless; we keep the premium and sell a new put next week.
rules.title: What if the put finishes out of the money?

rules.action: Record the assignment and buy 100 shares per contract at the strike; the cost basis is the strike less the put's credit
rules.condition: At the expiry session's close, the stock's last trade is below the put's strike
rules.name: Put assigned
rules.rationale: The second leg starts: we now own the shares, bought lower than the price when we sold the put, and we sell calls on them from next week. There's no early assignment.
rules.summary: We're assigned and buy 100 shares at the strike with the cash set aside.
rules.title: What if the put finishes in the money?

rules.action: Record the call as expired at $0; keep the shares
rules.condition: At the expiry session's close, the stock's last trade is at or below the call's strike
rules.name: Call expires
rules.rationale: The premium lowers the cost basis of the shares we keep.
rules.summary: It expires worthless; we keep the premium and the shares, and sell a new call next week.
rules.title: What if the call finishes out of the money?

rules.action: Record the assignment and sell the 100 shares per contract at the strike; next week, sell a put again
rules.condition: At the expiry session's close, the stock's last trade is above the call's strike
rules.name: Called away
rules.rationale: The wheel completes a turn: the shares go at a price at or above the cost basis, so the cycle as a whole is profitable. There's no early assignment.
rules.summary: The shares are called away at the strike, and we start again with a put.
rules.title: What if the call finishes in the money?

rules.action: Mark every position at the bar's mid; no forced liquidation
rules.name: End of backtest
rules.rationale: Selling at the end would add a trade the strategy never chose.
rules.summary: Everything still held is valued at its last mid; nothing is sold.
rules.title: What happens at the end of the backtest?
